item.research_question: How does the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, combined with annealing temperature, influence the hierarchical phase decomposition, microhardness, and magnetic properties in AlCoFeNi-based high entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Arc melting of elemental pellets (99.9% purity) under argon atmosphere, followed by isothermal annealing at 600 °C and 1000 °C for 15 h and water quenching
item.test_conditions: Annealing at 600 °C/15 h and 1000 °C/15 h; characterization via SEM, TEM, APT, EBSD, Vickers microhardness, and magnetic measurements (Ms, Hc)
key_findings: AlCoFeNi annealed at 1000 °C forms a single ordered B2 phase with a microhardness of 406 VHN, saturation magnetization (Ms) of 111.6 emu/g, and coercivity (Hc) of 4.3 Oe.
AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C decomposes into a B2 matrix and fine Fe-Co rich BCC precipitates, increasing microhardness to 474 VHN and Hc to 14.5 Oe while reducing Ms to 99.8 emu/g.
Substituting 50% Co with Cr in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi induces phase separation into B2 + BCC even at 1000 °C, with Ms dropping to 42.2 emu/g and Hc rising to 39.4 Oe.

AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi annealed at 600 °C exhibits a hierarchical microstructure with multiple decomposition length scales: coarse micron-scale BCC lamellae, ~50–100 nm BCC precipitates, and ~3–5 nm BCC clusters.
The AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy annealed at 600 °C achieves the highest microhardness of 475 VHN due to the multi-scale hierarchical B2 + BCC decomposition.
Cr addition reduces saturation magnetization by more than 50% compared to the Cr-free alloy due to the antiferromagnetic nature of Cr.
Grain boundary phases in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi annealed at 1000 °C were identified as FCC, while those annealed at 600 °C included sigma phase (σ) enriched in Cr, Fe, and Co.
item.mechanism: The addition of Cr introduces a strong tendency for phase separation due to positive enthalpies of mixing in Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, and Ni-Cr binary systems, leading to miscibility gaps. Lower annealing temperatures reduce atomic mobility, refining the length scale of decomposition and promoting hierarchical precipitation of BCC phases within the B2 matrix.
item.limitations: The thermodynamic model (CALPHAD) predicted an FCC phase in AlCoFeNi at 1000 °C which was not observed experimentally, likely due to high nucleation barriers and sluggish kinetics. The detailed thermodynamic basis for Cr's influence on phase separation in complex multi-component alloys requires further analysis beyond the scope of this work.
item.future_work: Further detailed investigation is required to understand the relationship between B2 phase decomposition into a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure and the resulting coercivity. Additionally, the thermodynamic basis underlying the influence of Cr on phase separation in these complex concentrated multi-component alloys needs further analysis.
quotes: The substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution.
The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature.
The substitution of Co by Cr in these AlCo x Cr 1−x FeNi alloys has rather interesting consequences on the phase stability.
